newsitem.title: USA: Prison REIT CCA Realty a hit on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Prison REIT CCA Realty a hit on Wall Street.

text.p: Shares of CCA Prison Realty Trust jumped 35 percent on their first day of trading after the real estate investment trust's initial public offering.
Shares were up 7-1/2 to 28-1/2 in afternoon trading.

IPO analysts had expected the offering to be a hot one with robust demand. The Maryland company even boosted terms of the offering ahead of the sale, offering 18.5 million shares, up from an original estimate of 17 million, for $21 each. That was the high end of its price talk of $19 to $21.
The offering raised $388.5 million for the company before paying underwriting fees. J.C. Bradford was the lead underwriter of the offering.

Prison Realty says it aims to use $308.1 million of the proceeds to buy nine jail facilities from jail-operator Corrections Corp of America, which it will lease back to Corrections Corp, according to its prospectus.
Corrections Corp is based in Nashville, Tennessee.

The company's chief executive, J. Michael Quinlan, is the former director of the Federal Bureau of Prisons. He left the bureau in 1992. For the last three years, he has been director of strategic planning at Corrections Corp.
The company has a limited operating history -- it was formed just last month -- on April 23, 1997.

Prison Realty plans to buy more facilities in the future to build on the growing trend towards privatization in corrections. At first it plans to focus on facilities operated by Corrections Corp (CCA) but could buy correction centers owned and operated by government entities, it said.

Prison Realty has several other close ties to CCA -- its new chairman Doctor R. Crants co-founded CCA in 1983 and has been its chief executive officer and chairman since June 1994. His 28-year-old son, D. Robert Crants III, will be the president of the new company. According to the prospectus, the younger Crants was at Goldman Sachs between 1990 and 1996 structuring over $3 billion in real estate transactions and over $1.0 billion in REIT public offerings.
